lessons.title: Prime Factorisation and HCF
lessons.summary: Connect prime factorisation with HCF and LCM.
learning_objectives: Use prime factors to calculate HCF and LCM

content_blocks.text: Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes. Compare the powers of common primes to find the HCF.
HCF uses the smaller powers; LCM uses the larger powers.

concepts.title: Prime factorisation
concepts.explanation: Writing a number as a product of prime numbers.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT Mathematics Class X, Chapter 1, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.explanation: 36 = 2²×3² and 84 = 2²×3×7, so the common product is 12.

lessons.title: Proving a Number Is Irrational
lessons.summary: Use proof-by-contradiction to show that √2 is irrational.
learning_objectives: Explain what an irrational number is

content_blocks.text: A rational number can be written as p/q in lowest terms. Irrational numbers cannot — so to prove √2 is irrational we assume it is rational and show that the assumption forces a contradiction.
Assume √2 = p/q with p and q coprime. Squaring gives 2q² = p², so p is even. Writing p = 2k gives q² = 2k², making q even too — both even contradicts them being coprime.
Whenever assuming rationality leads to a contradiction, the number must be irrational.

concepts.title: Irrationality by contradiction
concepts.explanation: Assume the number is rational, derive a contradiction, conclude it is irrational.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT Mathematics Class X, Chapter 1, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.prompt: Is the product of two irrational numbers always irrational? Give one counterexample.
questions.answer: No — for example √2 × √2 = 2, which is rational.
questions.explanation: The product of two irrationals can be rational (√2·√2) or irrational (√2·√3).

chapters.title: Polynomials
chapters.summary: Relate zeroes of a polynomial to its graph and coefficients.
chapters.source_reference: NCERT Mathematics Class X, Chapter 2, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

lessons.title: Reading Zeroes from a Graph
lessons.summary: Interpret x-intercepts as zeroes of a polynomial.
learning_objectives: Verify the relationship between zeroes and coefficients

content_blocks.text: A zero of p(x) is an x-value where p(x) = 0. On a graph, these are the points where the curve meets the x-axis.
For x² − 5x + 6, the zeroes are 2 and 3 because (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0.
The sum of zeroes is −b/a and their product is c/a for ax²+bx+c.

concepts.title: Zeroes
concepts.explanation: Values of x for which a polynomial evaluates to zero.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT Mathematics Class X, Chapter 2, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

lessons.title: Zeroes and the Coefficients of a Polynomial
lessons.summary: Link the sum and product of zeroes to the coefficients of a quadratic.

content_blocks.text: For ax² + bx + c with zeroes α and β: α + β = −b/a and αβ = c/a. This holds for every quadratic whose zeroes are real.
For x² − 5x + 6, α + β = 5 and αβ = 6, so the zeroes are the factor pair 2 and 3.
Coefficient relationships let you check factorisation quickly and rebuild a polynomial from its zeroes.

concepts.title: Zero-coefficient relationship
concepts.explanation: Sum and product of zeroes are fixed by the coefficients.

lessons.source_reference: NCERT Mathematics Class X, Chapter 2, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
